mappings.rationale: The medians determine midpoint and concurrency relationships. Their perpendicularity can be used through centroid ratios and similarity, or through midpoint coordinates and a zero dot product.
mappings.answerReason: Let G be the intersection of the medians. Then BG=(2/3)BN. Right triangles BGC and BCN are similar, since they share the angle at B, so BC²=BG·BN=(2/3)BN². With BC=s, this gives BN=s√6/2.

routes.label: Right-triangle projections and a difference formula

mappings.rationale: The alley width is the sum of the ladder's two horizontal projections. Alternatively, the two ladder positions form an equilateral triangle, allowing congruent right triangles to identify the width with h.
mappings.answerReason: The projections give w=a(cos75°+cos45°) and h=a sin75°. Expanding sin(75°-45°)=sin30° gives sin75°-cos75°=cos45°. Therefore w=a sin75°=h.

mappings.rationale: The two secants through each triangle vertex give equal external-times-whole products. Equal triangle sides connect these products and determine the separation of D and E.
mappings.answerReason: AC=16. Power at A gives AH(AH+7)=2·15=30, so AH=3, BJ=6, and BH=13. Put x=BD and y=BE. Powers at B and C give xy=78 and (16-x)(16-y)=14, hence x+y=20. Thus DE²=(y-x)²=20²-4·78=88, so DE=2√22.

mappings.rationale: Arrival probabilities are accumulated over incoming streets. Interior choices split probability equally, while moves forced along the boundary carry the full arrival probability; complete paths are not equally likely.
mappings.answerReason: Use grid coordinates counting east and south steps: A=(0,0), C=(3,3), B=(3,4). Adding incoming probabilities with half-weights at interior choices and full weights at forced exits gives p(3,2)=1/2 and p(2,3)=5/16. Therefore p(C)=1/2+(1/2)(5/16)=21/32.

mappings.rationale: Drawing BE decomposes the concave hexagon into two parallelograms. Equal parallel opposite sides establish those parallelograms, and the given 60° angles determine their heights.
mappings.answerReason: ABEF and BCDE are parallelograms because each has a pair of equal parallel opposite sides. Their adjacent sides all have length 1, and each has an included angle of 60°. Each area is 1·sin60°=√3/2, so the total area is √3.

mappings.rationale: Complex reciprocation conjugates the argument and replaces the modulus by its reciprocal. The task requires interpreting these changes in the displayed complex plane.
mappings.answerReason: F lies in the first quadrant outside the unit circle. If F=x+iy, then 1/F=(x-iy)/(x²+y²), which lies in the fourth quadrant and has modulus less than 1. Point C is the only displayed point satisfying both conditions.

mappings.rationale: The common tangent lines place the centers on an angle bisector. Homothety about the lines' intersection and consecutive external tangency force a constant adjacent radius ratio, making the middle radius a geometric mean.
mappings.answerReason: Distances of the centers from the wedge vertex are proportional to their radii. Combined with the external-tangency condition, this fixes the same ratio q between adjacent radii. Thus 18=8q⁴ and the middle radius is 8q²=√(8·18)=12.

mappings.rationale: Subtracting the shared triangle BDE turns the stated equality into equal areas on base DE. Equal heights then force DE parallel to AC, so proportional segments determine the requested area.
mappings.answerReason: Subtracting [BDE] gives [ADE]=[FDE]. Since A and F lie on the same side of DE, their perpendicular distances to DE are equal, so AF, and hence AC, is parallel to DE. Therefore BE/BC=BD/BA=3/5. Triangles ABE and ABC share the altitude to BC, giving [ABE]=(3/5)·10=6.
